task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 -- WRITE THE REGRESSION TESTS for the ISS-0109 fixture work. Both gates have
PASSed the implementation (SECURITY-REVIEWER step-03c, REVIEWER step-03d); no rework is owed.

BUILD FROM THE DESIGN'S FAIL-FIRST SECTION. The gate-approved design is lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md -- its
FAIL-FIRST PROVABILITY section enumerates cases C1 through C6 and is what you implement. Note
the design was corrected after the idiom gate: SS3.2's schema_state now types
registration_present? and schema_present? as `boolean() | nil`, where **false means
observed-absent and nil means not-observed**. Assert against that distinction; a test that
treats nil and false as interchangeable would erase the very property the correction exists to
protect.

WRITE: a test spec at test/specs/ISS-0109.md and the test code itself. The module under test is
test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (Letflow.TenantFixture).

READ THE WF-03 FAIL-FIRST RULE CAREFULLY, BECAUSE THE LITERAL FORM OF IT DOES NOT APPLY HERE AND
YOU MUST NOT FAKE IT. WF-03 Step 4 normally requires checking out the pre-fix commit, running the
new test, and confirming it FAILS there. That is impossible for this run in the literal sense:
the "fix" is a NEW MODULE that does not exist pre-fix, so a test calling it would not compile
rather than fail meaningfully, and a non-compiling test is not a fail-first proof of anything.

What the fail-first property actually means here -- and what your spec must state explicitly and
honestly -- is that the PRE-FIX DETECTION IS ABSENT, demonstrated on the broken state itself:
the old fixture asserted only that replay_migrations/1 returned {:ok, _}, and that assertion
PASSES against a schema missing a table. This is already MEASURED, twice, and you should cite the
measurements rather than re-deriving them from argument:
  - CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, step-02b: after dropping promotion_assertion_runs while leaving
    version 20260818090001 recorded, a second replay_migrations/1 returned {:ok, []} and the
    table was still absent.
  - ELIXIR-DEV, step-03: the same state through the new capture yields
    tables_missing: ["promotion_assertion_runs"], versions_missing: [].
So: the old assertion says fine, the new one says missing, on identical database state. THAT is
the regression proof. State it in the spec in those terms. Do NOT claim a pre-fix run of the new
test file, and do NOT dress a green post-fix run up as fail-first evidence.

Where a case CAN be shown to fail first in the ordinary way -- by mutating the new module and
observing the intended test go red -- that is stronger, and the design's SS7 says which cases
qualify. Use it where it applies.

BINDING INSTRUCTION FROM REVIEWER'S STEP-03D RULING 3, which exists specifically to stop you
writing a test that fails for the wrong reason: the SS3.3 ORACLE-ROT TEST MUST READ ITS OBSERVED
SET FROM capture_schema_state/1's `tables_present` -- NOT by querying information_schema.tables
itself. tables_present deliberately excludes schema_migrations (its contents are captured
separately as applied_versions), and expected_tenant_tables/0 excludes it too, so both-direction
set equality holds unfiltered. A raw catalog read WOULD return schema_migrations and would fail
that equality spuriously. The guard must fail in BOTH directions: a table added to the manifest
but not the oracle, AND a table removed from the manifest but left in the oracle.

ALSO REQUIRED:
- SS7.7's item has NO fail-first proof by construction (the two modules' adoption of the helper is
  a zero-behaviour-delta refactor). The design already declares this. Do not invent a test that
  pretends otherwise; the evidence for that item is the before/after module runs ELIXIR-DEV already
  captured (8 and 12 passing before, 8 and 12 after), which TEST-RUNNER will re-derive.
- Cover the capture's failure boundary per SS3.5, including the case that matters most: a degraded
  tables_present must yield tables_missing == [] and NOT "all 19 missing" -- an unobserved set must
  never be reported as an observed absence. Same rule for applied_versions/versions_missing.
- Cover the teardown log line: the literal LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE marker, a phase from the closed
  vocabulary, and schema_present_before_drop, under CaptureLog.
- Cover the negative case: a wholly absent tenant returns {:ok, state} with the present? flags
  false and does NOT raise (INV-F-4).

TEST NAME LENGTH: keep every test name under 255 characters. This repo has broken its own full
suite FOUR times on ExUnit's 255-char limit (see docs/anti-patterns.md and PR #351). Measure the
longest name mechanically before you finish -- do not eyeball it -- and report the measured
maximum.

DO NOT: modify test/support/tenant_fixture.ex or either adopted module (both gates passed them;
changing them would invalidate those verdicts). Do not touch the other 39 fixture sites
(ISS-0112). Do not fix ISS-0110/0111/0113/0107.

TOOLCHAIN: plain `mix compile` only -- no --warnings-as-errors, no `mix format` (Elixir 1.20.3/OTP
29 against a 1.18.3-otp-27 pin, ISS-0106, filed and not yours). Postgres for this workspace is on
LETFLOW_DB_PORT from ./.env. You write the tests; TEST-RUNNER runs the suite at Step 4b -- but you
should still compile and run YOUR OWN new tests to confirm they work, and quote that output.
Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by explicit filename, never `git add -A`. Note handoffs/orchestrator.log
belongs to ORCH -- leave it alone, and `git fetch` rather than pulling if a rebase refuses.
acceptance_criteria: test/specs/ISS-0109.md exists and maps every design FAIL-FIRST case (C1..C6) to a named test

The spec states the fail-first position HONESTLY: that the literal pre-fix-run form does not apply because the fix is a new module, that the real proof is the absence of pre-fix detection on identical database state, and it cites the two existing measurements (step-02b's {:ok, []} replay and step-03's tables_missing capture) rather than claiming a pre-fix run of the new test file
The SS3.3 oracle-rot test reads its observed set from capture_schema_state/1's tables_present, NOT from a raw information_schema.tables query, and fails in BOTH directions
C1 is implemented: a table dropped while its migration version remains recorded is detected by the completeness assertion
The SS3.5 failure boundary is covered, including that a degraded tables_present yields tables_missing == [] rather than a false 'all missing', and the same for applied_versions/versions_missing
The boolean() | nil distinction is asserted as a distinction: false (observed-absent) and nil (not-observed) are not treated as interchangeable
The teardown log line is covered under CaptureLog: literal marker, closed-vocabulary phase, schema_present_before_drop
The INV-F-4 negative case is covered: a wholly absent tenant returns {:ok, state} with present? flags false and does not raise
Every test name is under 255 characters, verified MECHANICALLY, with the measured maximum reported
test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and both adopted test modules are unmodified, and no other fixture site is touched
The new tests were compiled and run, with real output quoted

result.summary: Regression tests for Letflow.TenantFixture written and run. Spec: test/specs/ISS-0109.md. Tests: test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs -- 14 tests covering design SS7's C1..C6. FAIL-FIRST POSITION, stated honestly and not faked: the literal pre-fix-run form does not apply because the fix is a NEW MODULE (pre-fix the test file would not compile, which is evidence about nothing); no pre-fix run of this file is claimed anywhere, and the green post-fix run is not offered as fail-first evidence. The real property -- pre-fix detection absent on identical database state -- is cited from the two existing measurements (step-02b's second replay_migrations/1 returning {:ok, []} with promotion_assertion_runs still absent; step-03's tables_missing: ["promotion_assertion_runs"], versions_missing: [] through the new capture) AND re-derived mechanically in test C1.2, which runs the pre-fix fixture's entire oracle (assert {:ok, []} = replay_migrations/1) on the constructed state, confirms the table is still absent, then shows assert_schema_complete!/2 raising on that same state. SS7.7's adoption item is declared as having no fail-first proof; its evidence is behaviour preservation (20 passed = 8 + 12 for the two adopted modules, re-run here, matching ELIXIR-DEV's before/after). REVIEWER step-03d ruling 3 honoured: the C6 oracle-rot test reads its observed set from capture_schema_state/1's tables_present, never a raw information_schema.tables query, and fails in both directions (expected -- observed == [] AND observed -- expected == []). The boolean() | nil distinction is asserted AS a distinction: false (observed-absent) at tests 3 and 7, nil (not-observed) at test 9 with an explicit `refute == false` alongside `assert == nil`, and INV-F-10 at test 10 (a degraded capture returns :ok rather than reddening a healthy tenant). SS3.5's failure boundary is covered on both sides: a degraded tables_present yields tables_missing == [] rather than 'all 19 missing', a degraded applied_versions yields versions_missing == [] rather than all 31 manifest versions (constructed two ways -- a dropped schema, and an aborted transaction that makes every per-field query raise at once), and {:error, {:capture_failed, _}} is shown reachable only outside the field guards (malformed tenant_id). Teardown log line covered: exactly one line with the literal LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE marker, phase=teardown from the closed vocabulary, schema=, tenant_id=, schema_present_before_drop=true; ExUnit.CaptureLog cannot wrap an on_exit/1-driven teardown (it installs/removes its handler around a call in the test body, and the teardown runs after the test process exits), so that one line is observed via a marker-filtered :logger handler installed and read from LIFO-ordered on_exit callbacks -- the spec states this explicitly -- while the failure-phase lines, which are emitted synchronously, ARE asserted under capture_log/1 (phase=incomplete_schema present, phase=teardown absent, both during a failure and during a successful fixture run). INV-F-4's negative case covered: a wholly absent tenant returns {:ok, state} with both present? flags false and does not raise. TEST NAME LENGTH measured mechanically over the full 'test <describe> <name>' string ExUnit builds: MAXIMUM 140 characters (141 bytes; one name contains a section sign), 115 characters of headroom under ExUnit's 255 limit. RUN OUTPUT: `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs --seed 7` -> 'Finished in 7.6 seconds (0.00s async, 7.6s sync) / Result: 14 passed'; also green at seed 0 (10.9s) and seed 424242 (8.9s), so no test depends on ExUnit's shuffled order. No compiler warning originates from the new file (two that initially did -- a redundant is_exception/1 and a `!= nil` on a non-nullable field -- were replaced with stronger assertions). test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and both adopted modules are byte-for-byte unmodified (`git diff HEAD` on all three is empty); no other fixture site touched.
result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-03 Step 4a) to re-derive C1..C6 coverage independently, then TEST-RUNNER (Step 4b) for the full suite.
